items.excerpt: ## Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic files papers to sell shares to the public for the first time SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic filed papers Monday to sell shares to the public for the first time. The filing sets up the San Francisco company for a Wall Street debut next month in what could be the biggest ever initial public sale of stock. ## Lula’s win in Brazil bucks a regional shift to the right and denies Trump a powerful ally BUENOS AIRES, Argentina (AP) — Brazilian voters have denied Latin America’s resurgent right its ultimate prize. Leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated Flávio Bolsonaro with 51.8% of the vote in Sunday's runoff election. Lula's reelection limits U.S. President Donald Trump’s influence in the region and cements Brazil as a counterweight to Washington. Analysts say Lula’s victory complicates Trump’s campaign to enlist Brazil in a military coalition against cartels. Both sides see reasons to cooperate, with Washington seeking access to Brazil’s rare earths and Lula wanting foreign investment. Lula’s pragmatic approach may lead to cooperation despite political differences. ## Whatever the outcome of Israel's election, its policies toward the Palestinians will largely endure JALUD, West Bank (AP) — Tuesday's elections could end Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's political career. But his legacy in the occupied West Bank will likely endure. Over the last four years, his government has massively expanded Israeli settlements, displaced tens of thousands of Palestinians and empowered extremist settlers. His opponents promise to dismantle the most contentious settler outposts and rein in the violence. But they largely support Israel's broader settlement enterprise and are opposed to the establishment of a Palestinian state in territories occupied by Israel in the 1967 Mideast war. ## Serbia's political veteran Vucic outplayed all opponents. Then the students came BELGRADE, Serbia (AP) — Serbia’s populist leader Aleksandar Vucic has dominated politics in the Balkan country for 14 years. Then came the students. The former authoritarian president on Sunday the conceded defeat of his right-wing Serbian Progressive Party to a grassroots movement of university students who led protests against him for almost two years before unseating him in a historic change of government. The 56-year-old political veteran in the past had easily outplayed political opponents easily. Ahead of Sunday’s ballot he had pulled a maneuver in the style of Russian President Vladimir Putin, He resigned the presidency and launched a fierce campaign ## Trump escalates anti-Muslim attacks against El-Sayed in Michigan, drawing Arab American rebuke PORT HURON, Mich. (AP) — President Donald Trump is intensifying his anti-Muslim rhetoric against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed. He portrayed him during a Sunday rally in Port Huron as a threat to national security and questioned his loyalty to the United States. The remarks drew a sharp rebuke from a former top Arab American ally. Bishara Bahbah, a founder of Arab Americans for Trump, said the president's comments were racist. El-Sayed, who could become the nation’s first Muslim senator, faces Republican Mike Rogers in one of the races that will help determine control of the U.S. Senate in this year's midterms. ## Blanche says Trump isn't trying to meddle with Alaska election results by suing over Senate race WASHINGTON (AP) — Attorney General Todd Blanche is defending the Trump administration’s lawsuit to block certification of Alaska's Senate results if incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan loses the race. Blanche says the legal challenge filed last week was a necessary step to avoid confusing voters in the closely watched midterm race. Trump says he told his administration to file the case. Republicans fear that a second candidate on the ballot who is named Dan Sullivan could siphon away votes from the senator and tip the outcome in favor of Democrat Mary Peltola. That Dan Sullivan is a retired teacher and school administrator from a tiny fishing community. ## Venezuela's opposition leader Machado returns after months in exile, as doubts over democracy deepen CARACAS, Venezuela (AP) — Nobel laureate María Corina Machado has reappeared in Venezuela for the first time since December. She announced her return on social media, saying, “I am here. With you.” Opposition leader Edmundo Gonzalez confirmed her arrival and expressed support. He emphasized the importance of her return for Venezuelans. Machado's homecoming comes amid growing concerns about Venezuela's democratic future. Since the U.S. military deposed Nicolás Maduro, acting President Delcy Rodríguez has led the country. Rodríguez, a Maduro ally, has exceeded her authorized term, and no election is scheduled.

items.title: Fed to hit pause on rate hikes, but maybe not for long By Reuters
items.excerpt: Oct 26 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve policymakers have telegraphed they will not raise US short-term borrowing costs again this week, but with inflation concerns still front and center, investors believe a rate-hike pause will not last for long. Data due just one day after the Fed’s anticipated decision to hold rates steady in the 3.75%-4.00% range will underscore why. Inflation picked up last month and broadened well beyond rising fuel prices, and US economic growth accelerated last quarter, government reports are expected to show, with gains powered by solid consumer spending and surging business investment driven by demand for AI. Meanwhile the labor market has been stable: The unemployment rate was 4.2% last month and weekly unemployment insurance claims are running lower than at any point in Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh’s lifetime. ... Indeed, analysts say, were it not for a sharp rise in US Treasury yields in the weeks following the Fed’s September rate hike, a second straight increase this week would have been in the cards. "The data, in my opinion, do support a rate hike," said Nationwide Chief Economist Kathy Bostjancic, noting that data since the Fed’s last meeting showed "a strong economy, a strong consumer and labor market, and inflation ... deteriorated, it went the wrong way." ... Fed policymakers were "spooked" by a rise in US 10-year Treasury yields to near-quarter-century highs that threatened to slow the economy ... Financial markets responded by slashing bets on a rate hike. As of Friday, rate futures were pricing a 90% chance of a hold at the Fed’s October 27-28 meeting. ... There are data points the Fed can reasonably cite as justifying a pause, including hourly wage growth tracking below inflation for the last six months, showing the labor market is not adding much to inflation pressures. ... For his part, he said, Anderson now expects two more rate hikes from the Fed to contain inflation, which Fed officials target at 2% by the 12-month change in the personal consumption expenditures price index. ... September’s reading is not due until Thursday, but economists project it accelerated to 3.6% from 3.4% in August amid higher gas prices from the Middle East conflict, but also lifted by broader price pressures including from airfares, rents and computers.

items.title: U.S. Treasury yields: investors look ahead to the Fed's rate decision
items.excerpt: U.S. Treasury yields were flat on the day Monday as investors look ahead to the central bank's interest rate decision and await a flurry of economic data this week. The benchmark 10-year Treasury Add To Watchlist yield was up around 1 basis point at 4.99%, and the 30-year Treasury Add To Watchlist bond yield was unchanged at 5.31%. The 2-year Treasury Add To Watchlist note yield ticked 2 basis points higher to 4.7%. One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions. Investors are keenly anticipating the main event of the week, which will be the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on Wednesday. Traders are pricing in an over 90% chance that policymakers will hold interest rates steady at the current target range of 3.75% to 4%, per the CME FedWatch Tool. Deutsche Bank analysts said they expect there to be more interest in Chairman Kevin Warsh's comments following the decision, with focus on how the Fed "balances still-elevated inflation and solid growth against the recent tightening in financial conditions." "The broader message is still likely to be hawkish: our economists think recent inflation data support the case for further tightening over time, even if the Fed chooses to pause this week," the analysts said in a Monday note. ... They added that Warsh is expected to clarify that tight financial conditions are not a substitute for higher policy rates. ... Investors will also closely monitor the personal consumption expenditures index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, which will be released on Thursday. ... Other economic data to be published this week includes the weekly ADP Employment Change and durable goods Orders for September on Tuesday; weekly initial jobless claims on Thursday; and further employment data on Friday.

items.title: US business activity cools in October; strong demand fueling price pressures By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US business activity slowed modestly in October, though robust demand allowed companies to raise prices for goods and services, a sign that inflation could increase further and remain persistently high in the coming months. S&P Global said on Friday its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, slipped to 57.6 this month from a five-year high reading of 58.4 in September. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector. Strength in manufacturing was offset by a slight pullback in the vast services sector. The PMI suggested the economy started the fourth quarter on solid footing following what is expected to have been a strong performance in the July-September quarter. Economists expect the government’s advance gross domestic product report next week to show the economy growing at around a 3.0% annualized rate last quarter, mainly driven by consumer spending and business investment in AI. ... items.excerpt: PORT HURON, Mich. — President Donald Trump intensified his anti-Muslim rhetoric against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday, portraying him as a threat to national security and questioning his loyalty to the United States in remarks that drew a sharp rebuke from a former top Arab American ally. Trump called El-Sayed, a former Detroit health official, a "jihadist" who was "on the side of the terrorists" and would "have to go through a metal detector before he's allowed to go into the Senate." He also repeatedly invoked the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, drawing a comparison between stopping El-Sayed from entering the Senate chamber and the passengers who fought back against the hijackers aboard United Flight 93. El-Sayed, who would become the nation's first Muslim senator if elected, has called attacks on his loyalty to the country "shameful" and repeatedly denied any ties to extremist groups. The Republican president's remarks were condemned by Bishara Bahbah, a founder of Arab Americans for Trump, the group that helped lead the president's outreach to Arab American voters in 2024.

items.title: Idina Menzel, Adam Pascal, Anthony Rapp and More Join RENT 30th Anniversary Concert
items.excerpt: Twelve original cast members and three decades of alumni will light up Broadway at Rent, the 30th Anniversary Concert, a benefit performance in celebration of the landmark Tony Award- and Pulitzer Prize-winning rock musical. The one-night-only concert performance of the full show will take place Monday, October 26, 2026, at Broadway's Richard Rodgers Theatre and benefit Broadway Cares/Equity Fights AIDS. While in-person tickets are sold out, $30 livestream tickets are available for theater lovers worldwide to experience the revolutionary power of Rent. More than 50 Rent all-stars and special guests will take the stage to commemorate Jonathan Larson's groundbreaking musical sensation. Rent's original director, five-time Tony Award nominee Michael Greif, will return to helm the evening ... Original Rent cast members returning to the roles they made famous are Tony winner Idina Menzel, Tony nominee Adam Pascal, Anthony Rapp, Tony nominee Daphne Rubin-Vega, Tony winner Wilson Jermaine Heredia and Fredi Walker, as well as Yassmin Alers, Gilles Chiasson, Shelley Dickinson, David Driver, Darius de Haas and Rodney Hicks.
